integrity: For an unmatched vertex on either side, its universal opposite-side neighborhood forces every opposite-side color class to be odd. A color class containing a matched endpoint cannot contain another vertex on that side because the paired nonneighbor sees an even positive number of that color. Properness restricts cross-part reuse to the deleted matched pairs. These necessary and sufficient rules yield the exact counting polynomial and minima. A definition-level finite verifier checks the full coloring profile and independent constructions.
scientific_limitations: The graph must be a complete bipartite graph with a nonempty matching deleted that covers neither bipartition side.
The exact polynomial does not apply unchanged to the complete-bipartite endpoint or the full crown endpoint.
The core theorem follows from a symbolic color-class argument; finite enumerations only corroborate it.
Differently named or non-indexed coverage may exist; no claim of complete database coverage is made.
title: Strong odd coloring profiles of partially deleted complete bipartite graphs
